model.comment: This example demonstrates the Hybrid (Measure & Move) approach with datum-based constraints

constraints.description: Datum planes on inside jaw surfaces - measures at datums, moves parts
Datum points at pivot centers - ensures perfect alignment, moves parts
Datum plane on base top surface - measures at datum, moves base (soft constraint)

comment_instructions: HYBRID (MEASURE & MOVE) APPROACH:
- entities: The parts that will be moved/rotated by the constraint
- datums: Optional datum planes/points for precise measurement
- When datums specified: constraint measures at datum locations but moves parent parts
- Datums automatically follow their parent parts via scene graph hierarchy
DATUM ELEMENT NAMING:
- jaw_left_grip_plane: Datum plane on inside gripping surface of left jaw
- jaw_right_grip_plane: Datum plane on inside gripping surface of right jaw
- jaw_left_pivot_point: Datum point at center of left jaw pivot hole
- jaw_right_pivot_point: Datum point at center of right jaw pivot hole
- base_reference_plane: Datum plane on top surface of base platform
HOW TO CREATE IN SOLIDWORKS:
1. Open part in Part Design mode
2. Insert → Reference Geometry → Plane/Point/Axis
3. Define using existing faces/edges/vertices
4. Right-click in tree → Rename with descriptive name (use underscores, no spaces)
5. Export assembly as GLB with 'Include Reference Geometry' option enabled
6. Datum elements will export as separate named nodes in GLB file
WHY THIS WORKS:
- Datums export as child nodes in the scene graph
- Constraint measures orientation/position at datum node
- But applies transformation to PARENT part node
- Since datum is child of part, it automatically follows when part moves
- Result: Precise sub-element constraint without complex inverse kinematics!
See SOLIDWORKS_DATUM_TUTORIAL.md for detailed step-by-step instructions
